Subject: Next steps: econ buyer identification + procurement contact for VetraHealth

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the team on the call earlier. Quick recap and the items we committed to:

- Recap: demo of Redwood inference runtime, expected throughput for your 3k daily-concurrent users, and quantization options we discussed.
- Action for you: confirm the economic buyer / budget owner and procurement/legal contacts so we can loop them into the commercial conversation.
- Action for us: circle back with a pricing band for a 3-month pilot, and a short procurement checklist to speed legal/procurement review.

Couple of clarifying questions that will help us prepare the pilot SOW and pricing:
1) Who is the budget owner for platform spend — finance, product, or a centralized cloud team?
2) Does VetraHealth require US-only data residency and an on-prem option for PHI workloads?
3) Any minimum contract terms your procurement team expects (PO process, signature authority threshold)?

If you can intro the econ buyer + procurement lead on a single thread I’ll propose a 30-minute intro slot and attach a short list of what procurement typically asks for (SOC2 evidence, KMS pattern, SLA language).

I’ve attached the call notes / requirements grid we captured (VetraHealth_requirements_grid.xlsx) for reference.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with Evan or Priya if you want to accelerate.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Connor — thanks for the recap and for the notes. Small clarification on our side:

- Econ / budget owner: Evan Li (CFO) — he owns platform spend decisions for pilots and POC budgets.
- Procurement lead: Priya Mehta (priya.mehta@vetrahealth.com) — handles vendor paperwork and PO flow.
- Decision criteria: latency <200ms 95th percentile, SOC2 Type II, and clear data isolation for PHI.
- Pilot budget: we have ~USD 200k carved out for a 3-month pilot (covers infra + license).

Priya — looping you here. Can you confirm your standard procurement timeline (how long your security questionnaire review usually takes) and whether we need a vendor form filled out?

Connor — can you send a ballpark figure for the pilot (order-of-magnitude) and a short checklist we can forward to security & procurement? If we look like a fit, Evan is happy to do a 30-min call next week to review the business case.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, VetraHealth
alex.sanders@vetrahealth.com

Connor / team — attaching our standard procurement & provisioning checklist which enumerates the minimal items procurement/security will ask for. In brief:
- SOC2 Type II report (we provide a trimmed evidence pack)
- KMS integration notes (we support customer-managed keys via common cloud KMS vendors)
- SLA & uptime commitments for Dedicated vs Hosted plans
- Data residency options and on-prem packaging notes

Pricing note (order-of-magnitude for a 3-month pilot): USD 120k–220k depending on Dedicated v Hosted and token volumes (this aligns with the budget Alex mentioned). We suggest we surface a scoped SOW + PO flow for procurement to review.

Priya / Evan — happy to jump on a call this week to walk through checklist items. If you want, Connor can send a calendar invite with two available 30-min windows.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
